links.targetTitle: Grove's treasury operations are governed by refilling rate l

title: Rate limits are replenishing buckets: a maximum amount plus a daily refill slope
content:
Every entry in A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.1.1.3 is expressed as a pair. `LIMIT_USDS_MINT`, for example, has `maxAmount`: 1,000,000,000 USDS and `slope`: 1,000,000,000 USDS per day; `LIMIT_USDC_TO_DOMAIN` on Base has maxAmount 4,000,000 USDC with slope 2,000,000 USDC per day.

The two numbers describe a replenishing bucket, not a cap. `maxAmount` is the largest amount available at any instant; `slope` is how fast spent capacity is restored. A Relayer that exhausts the bucket must wait for it to refill, so the limit bounds both a single action and the sustained rate of actions.

This is what makes delegating operational authority safe enough to be useful. A per-transaction cap can be defeated by repetition; a daily quota with no instantaneous bound permits one catastrophic move. The bucket bounds both, so the worst case from a compromised Relayer key is `maxAmount` immediately plus `slope` per day until the Freezer intervenes — a computable, time-bounded loss.

The ratio between the two numbers is itself a policy statement. Where slope is smaller than maxAmount (Base USDC: 4M available, 2M/day refill) the design tolerates a large one-off move but throttles repetition, so recovery takes days. Where slope equals maxAmount the full capacity returns every day, which favours operational freedom over containment.
description: Every limit carries both maxAmount and slope, so authority is a capacity that drains with use and refills over time rather than a static per-transaction cap.
